r1-observability-1.summary: notification-service experienced a sudden surge in error rate starting at 13:25 UTC on 2026-10-14, reaching over 24 percent. Logs show DNS resolution failures (getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN) for both sms-vendor.example.net and fcm.push-provider.example.com.

findings.statement: notification-service error rate metric spiked to 22.63% at 13:25:00 UTC and peaked at 26.58%
notification-service began logging DNS resolution errors for fcm.push-provider.example.com at 13:25:05 UTC
notification-service began logging DNS resolution errors for sms-vendor.example.net at 13:25:10 UTC

open_questions: Why did DNS resolution for external vendor endpoints fail specifically at 13:25 UTC?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped notification-service dependencies (async event-bus upstream, sync sms-vendor and push-provider downstream, plus coredns platform dependency) and reviewed 7 days of changes, identifying a coredns scale-down infrastructure change (chg-8542) at 13:22 UTC, immediately preceding the symptom onset at ~13:25 UTC.

findings.statement: notification-service depends synchronously on sms-vendor and push-provider, asynchronously on event-bus, and uses coredns for name resolution.
An infrastructure change chg-8542 scaled coredns replicas from 4 to 1 at 2026-10-14T13:22:00+00:00.
Symptom onset for intermittent notification failures began at ~13:25 UTC, which is 3 minutes after the coredns replica reduction.

open_questions: Did the reduction in coredns replicas lead to DNS resolution timeouts or failures when notification-service attempts to reach external vendors?

r2-observability-1.summary: CoreDNS scale-down (chg-8542) from 4 to 1 replica at 13:22 directly caused severe CPU saturation, high query latency p99, and high error rates starting at 13:23, leading to DNS timeouts and subsequent notification-service resolution failures.

findings.statement: CoreDNS replicas were scaled down from 4 to 1 at 2026-10-14T13:22:00+00:00 under chg-8542.
CoreDNS CPU percentage showed an anomaly starting at 13:23, peaking at 105.92% at 13:46.
CoreDNS latency p99 spiked upwards starting at 13:23, reaching a peak of 2112.52 ms.
CoreDNS error rate percentage showed an anomaly starting at 13:23, peaking at 22.72%.
CoreDNS logged UDP read i/o timeout errors starting at 13:24:03.

hypotheses.title: CoreDNS replica scale-down causes DNS resolution timeouts for external vendors
hypotheses.mechanism: Scaling coredns down from 4 to 1 replica reduced query capacity, causing CPU saturation, high latency, and UDP read i/o timeouts starting at 13:23-13:24. This led to DNS requests for external endpoints to fail with EAI_AGAIN starting at 13:25, causing notification-service delivery errors.

supporting.note: Precedes symptom onset by 3 minutes and directly reduces coredns capacity.
Shows coredns CPU saturation starting immediately after scale-down.
Shows high DNS latency starting at 13:23.
Shows coredns error rate spike starting at 13:23.
Coredns logged UDP read i/o timeout errors starting at 13:24.
Shows the exact onset of the error surge at 13:25 UTC.
Indicates DNS getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN failures for push-provider starting at 13:25 UTC.
Indicates DNS getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN failures for sms-vendor starting at 13:25 UTC.
Past incident confirms coredns configuration/capacity issues cause similar EAI_AGAIN errors across services.

contradicting.note: Request rate remained stable, meaning the trigger was structural capacity reduction rather than a traffic spike.

assumptions: Reducing coredns replicas from 4 to 1 left insufficient capacity to handle cluster DNS query load under normal operation.

hypotheses.title: External DNS or upstream resolver timeout coinciding with coredns replica change
hypotheses.mechanism: External DNS resolvers for sms-vendor and push-provider experienced transient failures at 13:25 UTC coincidentally right after the coredns scale-down.

supporting.note: Shows resolution errors specifically for push-provider.
Shows resolution errors specifically for sms-vendor.

contradicting.note: Proves internal coredns was severely resource-constrained at the exact same time.
Proves coredns latency spiked right before the notification errors.
Proves coredns itself was failing queries.
Shows coredns experiencing UDP read i/o timeouts.
The tight window after coredns change strongly points to the internal scaling change.
Simultaneous failure across two completely independent vendors points to a shared local resolver issue.

assumptions: Both external vendor DNS records experienced concurrent transient upstream resolution issues completely independent of the internal coredns resource saturation.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The critic noted in the previous round that coredns health metrics and logs were missing. With the retrieval of r2-observability-1 findings (metric:coredns:cpu_pct, metric:coredns:latency_p99_ms, metric:coredns:error_rate_pct, and log-00525), we now have direct, verified proof that the coredns scale-down (chg-8542) immediately triggered CPU saturation, high query latency, error rates, and UDP timeout errors starting at 13:23-13:24. This directly preceded the notification-service error spike at 13:25 (metric:notification-service:error_rate_pct, log-00531, log-00533). Hypothesis H1 confidence is raised to 0.92, while H2 remains very unlikely given the clear internal DNS bottleneck evidence.
